newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom not set on Eurobond - Gazprom consultant.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom not set on Eurobond - Gazprom consultant.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom will target foreign investors with a new bond, but not necessarily a Eurobond and probably not this year, the head of its financial consultancy said on Monday.

Leonid Gryaznov, chief executive of Gazprom consulting subsidiary Gorizont, told Reuters in an interview that Gazprom was considering issues of Eurobonds and Yankee bonds, intended for U.S. markets, to finance its Yamal pipeline.
"A number of possibilities are being considered... but no decision has been made," he said, adding that preparations for a bond, once a decision was taken, would probably take two months.
The Financial Times on Friday reported that Gazprom intended to issue a $250-500 million Eurobond.
Gryaznov said Gazprom intended to raise capital on foreign markets for its multi-billion dollar Yamal pipeline project to Western Europe.
"It would be possible, but difficult to do an issue in a month," he said.
"Everything depends on the domestic political situation. If everything goes well, then it is possible to speak about some kind of probability that it will happen before the end of the year," he said.
Gazprom would be able to speed new issues to the market thanks to experience gained during four months of preparation for its American Depositary Share issue in October which raised $429.3 million.

But Russian companies must wait on the government to make rules for issuing Eurobonds and might not be able to issue such foreign-currency-denominated bonds if the government is forced to issue its own Eurobond, expected this month, at high rates.
"The legislation does not yet exist... (and) the rates that the government presently offers on (domestic) bonds are simply unacceptable to most corporations," he said.
The six-month treasury bill yield at auction on October 31 averaged 53.09 percent.
"If (political) things go (poorly), then it is difficult to talk about time periods for issues."

But the firm will not issue convertible bonds over the next six months, he said, as Gazprom agreed not to issue "anything linked to shares" over that period without permission from the global coordinators of its ADS issue, Morgan Stanley and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
